extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A freely available benchmark dataset for language modeling that allows for learning long range dependencies and deals with more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora than Penn Treebank.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Articles were selected from Wikipedia based on Good or Featured article criteria, with text extracted using the Wikipedia API. The extraction process involved handling Wikipedia markup, removing specific sections with lists, cleaning bugs and leaked HTML elements, replacing mathematical formulae with tokens, and performing normalization and tokenization using the Moses tokenizer with augmentations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles classified as Good or Featured articles (23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles), which are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable according to Wikipedia editor criteria.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Penn Treebank has limitations including tokens that are all lower case, stripped of punctuation, and limited to a vocabulary of only 10k words. These limitations mean that PTB is unrealistic for real language use, especially when far larger vocabularies with many rare words are involved. The lack of a long tail for the vocabulary is problematic given that accurately predicting rare words, such as named entities, is an important task for many applications.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The WikiText dataset is intended for language modeling tasks, particularly for improving handling of rare words and the usage of long term dependencies in language modeling. It serves as a platform to move beyond Penn Treebank limitations.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be made available to the community.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token. Numbers were replaced with N in PTB preprocessing. Mathematical formulae and LATEX code were replaced with <formula> tokens.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Vocabulary constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. For PTB, vocabulary limited to most frequent 10k words with rest replaced by <unk> token. Specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text extraction from Wikipedia markup using Wikipedia API. Words were lower-cased. Newlines replaced with <eos>. Punctuation removed (PTB). Minor bugs like sort keys and Edit buttons removed. Normalization and tokenization performed using Moses tokenizer, augmented to further split numbers (8,600 → 8 @,@ 600).

name.evidence: we also introduce a new benchmark dataset for language modeling called WikiText

description.evidence: In order to evaluate how well language models can exploit longer contexts and deal with more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora we also introduce the freely available WikiText corpus... Since this commonly used dataset is small and no other freely available alternative exists that allows for learning long range dependencies, we also introduce a new benchmark dataset for language modeling called WikiText.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia... The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API. Extracting the raw text from Wikipedia mark-up is nontrivial due to the large number of macros in use... Once extracted, specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and LATEX code, were replaced with <formula> tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia. These articles have been reviewed by humans and are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers (8,600 !8 @,@ 600) and with some additional minor fixes.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The tokens in PTB are all lower case, stripped of any punctuation, and limited to a vocabulary of only 10k words. These limitations mean that the PTB is unrealistic for real language use, especially when far larger vocabularies with many rare words are involved... Given that accurately predicting rare words, such as named entities, is an important task for many applications, the lack of a long tail for the vocabulary is problematic.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We hope this new dataset can serve as a platform to improve handling of rare words and the usage of long term dependencies in language modeling.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Hence, we constructed a language modeling dataset using text extracted from Wikipedia and will make this available to the community.
